records.jp: あの……星崎さん。<CR>少し、相談したいことがあるんです
records.en_original: Um... Ao? There's something I'd like to speak with you about.
records.en_auxiliary: Um... Ao? There's something I'd like to speak with you about.
records.en: Um... Hoshizaki-san.<CR>There is something I would like to ask your advice about.

records.jp: 詩さん……なんだか暗い顔してる。<CR>どうしたの？
records.en_original: Uta? What's with the long face?
records.en_auxiliary: Uta? What's with the long face?
records.en: Uta-san... You look kind of gloomy.<CR>What is wrong?

records.jp: 少し、悩んでいることがあるんです。<CR>でも、星崎さんにしか話せない気がして……
records.en_original: There's...something that's been bothering me. I feel like you're the only person I can talk to about it...
records.en_auxiliary: There's...something that's been bothering me. I feel like you're the only person I can talk to about it...
records.en: There is something that has been troubling me.<CR>But I feel as though you are the only person I can tell, Hoshizaki-san...

records.jp: 話を聞いていただけますか？
records.en_original: Do you mind?
records.en_auxiliary: Do you mind?
records.en: Would you listen to me?

records.jp: うん。もちろんだよ
records.en_original: Of course not!
records.en_auxiliary: Of course not!
records.en: Yeah. Of course.

records.jp: ……ひまわり畑？
records.en_original: A sunflower field...?
records.en_auxiliary: A sunflower field...?
records.en: ...The sunflower field?

records.jp: はい。ここで話すのが良いと思いまして
records.en_original: Yes. I thought this would be a good place to talk.
records.en_auxiliary: Yes. I thought this would be a good place to talk.
records.en: Yes. I thought it would be best to speak here.

records.jp: （詩さんにとって……<CR>ひまわりは、おばあさんとの記憶……）
records.en_original: (Sunflowers... They must remind Uta of her grandmother.)
records.en_auxiliary: (Sunflowers... They must remind Uta of her grandmother.)
records.en: (For Uta-san...<CR>sunflowers are tied to her memories of her grandmother...)

records.jp: ……ココロトープで見た通り、<CR>私は、昔から人との共感が困難でした
records.en_original: As I'm sure you noticed while in my Heartscape, I've always had trouble relating to others.
records.en_auxiliary: As I'm sure you noticed while in my Heartscape, I've always had trouble relating to others.
records.en: ...As you saw in my Heartscape,<CR>I have always had difficulty empathizing with other people.

records.jp: 記憶を取り戻すまで、このひまわり畑を見る度に<CR>心に奇妙な揺らぎを感じました
records.en_original: Before I regained my memory, I felt a strange flutter in my heart whenever I saw this field of sunflowers.
records.en_auxiliary: Before I regained my memory, I felt a strange flutter in my heart whenever I saw this field of sunflowers.
records.en: Until I regained my memories, every time I saw this sunflower field,<CR>I felt a strange disturbance in my heart.

records.jp: ……私の過去にひまわり畑が深く関わっていたと<CR>知るまでは、何故だろうと思っていました
records.en_original: I had always wondered why, but I never would have guessed I had such a close connection with them.
records.en_auxiliary: I had always wondered why, but I never would have guessed I had such a close connection with them.
records.en: ...Until I learned that a sunflower field was deeply connected to my past,<CR>I wondered why I felt that way.

records.jp: おばあさんが、詩さんのために植えたんだよね
records.en_original: Your grandmother planted them for you, didn't she?
records.en_auxiliary: Your grandmother planted them for you, didn't she?
records.en: Your grandmother planted them for you, did she not, Uta-san?

records.jp: はい。私がひまわりを好きなのだと勘違いして、<CR>よくひまわりの話をして……
records.en_original: That's right. She mistakenly thought I liked sunflowers, and she often talked about them...
records.en_auxiliary: That's right. She mistakenly thought I liked sunflowers, and she often talked about them...
records.en: Yes. She mistakenly believed I liked sunflowers,<CR>and often spoke to me about them...

records.jp: 祖母は、私の心を勝手に推し測っては、<CR>見当違いな言葉をかけたり世話を焼いたり……
records.en_original: My grandmother would always assume things about me, never asking my opinion while she fussed over me.
records.en_auxiliary: My grandmother would always assume things about me, never asking my opinion while she fussed over me.
records.en: My grandmother would decide for herself what was in my heart,<CR>then say misguided things and fuss over me...

records.jp: あー、あるあるだよね。うちの親もたまに<CR>口うるさいし、変な勘違いもよくあるしさ
records.en_original: Ah, I know what you mean. My parents always nag me and misunderstand the weirdest things.
records.en_auxiliary: Ah, I know what you mean. My parents always nag me and misunderstand the weirdest things.
records.en: Ah, that kind of thing happens all the time. My parents sometimes<CR>nag me and make strange assumptions too.

records.jp: お世辞で褒めたご飯を好物だとか思われて、<CR>しばらくそればっかになるとかねー
records.en_original: Like if I say I like something they cooked, I end up eating it every day for months.
records.en_auxiliary: Like if I say I like something they cooked, I end up eating it every day for months.
records.en: Like when I compliment someone's cooking just to be polite,<CR>and they decide it's my favorite and keep serving it to me.

records.jp: 「あるある」……ですか？<CR>でも、私は……
records.en_original: Is that normal? But I...
records.en_auxiliary: Is that normal? But I...
records.en: It "happens all the time"...?<CR>But I...

records.jp: そんな祖母のことを煩わしく思い、<CR>祖母の死まで訪ねることすら避けました
records.en_original: I was so annoyed with my grandmother that I avoided visiting her all the way until her death.
records.en_auxiliary: I was so annoyed with my grandmother that I avoided visiting her all the way until her death.
records.en: I found my grandmother bothersome,<CR>and avoided even visiting her until she died.

records.jp: そして、祖母の葬儀のために、<CR>久々に家を訪れた時でした
records.en_original: The only time I visited after that was for the funeral.
records.en_auxiliary: The only time I visited after that was for the funeral.
records.en: Then, when I went back to her house for the first time in ages<CR>to attend her funeral...

records.jp: ……祖母の家の周りには、<CR>一面のひまわり畑ができていました
records.en_original: When I arrived, sunflowers had bloomed everywhere.
records.en_auxiliary: When I arrived, sunflowers had bloomed everywhere.
records.en: ...The whole area around my grandmother's house<CR>was covered in sunflowers.

records.jp: それじゃ、ココロトープで見た<CR>あのひまわり畑は……
records.en_original: So that's what we saw in your Heartscape...
records.en_auxiliary: So that's what we saw in your Heartscape...
records.en: Then the sunflower field<CR>we saw in your Heartscape...

records.jp: ……はい。元からあったものではありません。<CR>祖母が植えたものだったんです
records.en_original: ...That's right. They weren't always there. My grandmother planted them herself.
records.en_auxiliary: ...That's right. They weren't always there. My grandmother planted them herself.
records.en: ...Yes. It was not there originally.<CR>My grandmother had planted it.

records.jp: そう、だったんだ……
records.en_original: I see...
records.en_auxiliary: I see...
records.en: I see...

records.jp: （おばあさんはきっと、詩さんに喜んで<CR>もらいたくて、ひまわりを……）
records.en_original: (Her grandmother must have wanted to make Uta happy when she planted them...)
records.en_auxiliary: (Her grandmother must have wanted to make Uta happy when she planted them...)
records.en: (Her grandmother must have planted the sunflowers<CR>because she wanted to make Uta-san happy...)

records.jp: （あんなすごいひまわり畑にするまで、<CR>どのくらい時間や手間がかかったんだろう）
records.en_original: (She must have worked long and hard to grow that many sunflowers.)
records.en_auxiliary: (She must have worked long and hard to grow that many sunflowers.)
records.en: (How much time and effort must it have taken<CR>to make such an incredible sunflower field?)

records.jp: （それだけたくさん、<CR>詩さんのことを想ったんだろうな……でも）
records.en_original: (I'm sure she loved Uta a lot. But...)
records.en_auxiliary: (I'm sure she loved Uta a lot. But...)
records.en: (She must have thought about Uta-san<CR>that much... But...)

records.jp: でも私は、あの景色を見た瞬間に、そして<CR>思い出す度に、心がざわつくんです
records.en_original: But when I saw those flowers, and every time I remember it, my heart flutters.
records.en_auxiliary: But when I saw those flowers, and every time I remember it, my heart flutters.
records.en: But the instant I saw that sight, and every time<CR>I remember it, my heart becomes restless.

records.jp: そして、この感情の乱れの正体が<CR>ずっと理解できないままでいるんです
records.en_original: I've been unable to understand just what these emotions are.
records.en_auxiliary: I've been unable to understand just what these emotions are.
records.en: And I have remained unable to understand<CR>the true nature of this emotional disturbance.

records.jp: 私は、この気持ちが何なのか、知りたい……
records.en_original: I want to know what it is I'm feeling...
records.en_auxiliary: I want to know what it is I'm feeling...
records.en: I want to know what this feeling is...

records.jp: （おばあさんの詩さんへの想い……<CR>どうやったら詩さんに伝わるんだろう）
records.en_original: (How can I help Uta understand how her grandmother felt about her?)
records.en_auxiliary: (How can I help Uta understand how her grandmother felt about her?)
records.en: (Her grandmother's feelings for Uta-san...<CR>How can I make them reach her?)

records.jp: （いま私が話しても、多分伝わらない。<CR>ただの気持ちの押し付けになっちゃう気がする）
records.en_original: (I don't think just telling her would do any good. It would be no different from just forcing my own opinions on her.)
records.en_auxiliary: (I don't think just telling her would do any good. It would be no different from just forcing my own opinions on her.)
records.en: (Even if I explain them now, they probably will not reach her.<CR>I feel like I would only be imposing my own feelings on her.)

records.jp: （どうすれば、伝わるのかな……）
records.en_original: (How can I help her...?)
records.en_auxiliary: (How can I help her...?)
records.en: (How can I get through to her...?)

records.jp: ……あの、星崎さん。<CR>こんな話、迷惑……ですよね
records.en_original: Ao? I'm sorry, this is a bother, isn't it?
records.en_auxiliary: Ao? I'm sorry, this is a bother, isn't it?
records.en: ...Um, Hoshizaki-san.<CR>I'm bothering you with all this, aren't I?

records.jp: う、ううん。<CR>こんな大事な話を私にしてくれて、嬉しい
records.en_original: Not at all. I'm glad that you feel you can talk about this stuff with me.
records.en_auxiliary: Not at all. I'm glad that you feel you can talk about this stuff with me.
records.en: N-no.<CR>I am glad you shared something so important with me.

records.jp: 詩さんが私を信頼してくれてるって、<CR>そんな気がするから
records.en_original: It makes me feel like you trust me.
records.en_auxiliary: It makes me feel like you trust me.
records.en: Because it makes me feel<CR>that you trust me, Uta-san.

records.jp: いつかその気持ちの正体、きっと見つかるよ。<CR>私も、絶対に力になるからさ
records.en_original: I know you'll learn what that feeling is one day. I'll be there to help every step of the way.
records.en_auxiliary: I know you'll learn what that feeling is one day. I'll be there to help every step of the way.
records.en: I am sure we will discover what that feeling is someday.<CR>And I will definitely help you.

records.jp: 星崎さん……<CR>ありがとうございます
records.en_original: Ao... Thank you very much...
records.en_auxiliary: Ao... Thank you very much...
records.en: Hoshizaki-san...<CR>Thank you.

records.jp: （こんな適当な答えしか返せないなんて、<CR>……情けないなぁ、私）
records.en_original: (What a pathetic answer I gave her... I'm the worst.)
records.en_auxiliary: (What a pathetic answer I gave her... I'm the worst.)
records.en: (To think I could only give her such a vague answer...<CR>...How pathetic of me.)
